You are the REPORTER worker for the T9h hidden-clues smoke report repair in freytag-forge. Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Run Python as `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python` only (never uv; uv cannot run in your sandbox). Run tests with: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call, no billed call, no Worker, no credentials. Do not git commit. NO regular expressions in new code and never parse narration text to decide anything. Match the surrounding code's style, comment density and naming. The working tree already holds unrelated uncommitted edits by other people: touch ONLY the files you own and never run git checkout, git stash, git reset or git clean. At the end run `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix` and `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format` on the files you own. Player inputs in tests are imperative commands, e.g. `Look under the park bench.`, never first person. The tests you write must be hermetic (no live Worker) and few but complete: add a test only when it covers something useful in full, and update or delete existing tests whose old behaviour you are deliberately changing.

FILES YOU OWN (edit only these three): /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/hidden_clues_smoke_report.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_hidden_clues_smoke_report.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/docs/testing-runbook.md. You may READ anything. NEVER modify anything else.

BACKGROUND. `hidden_clues_smoke_report.py` turns a smoke run's rows.json and summary.json into gates S1-S6. Review found these defects. Read the report, its test file, and the producers that write the rows (grep for `state_digest_before` in scripts/ringer/environment_narration/make_t9h_route_e_harness_manifest.py and scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py) so you know exactly which typed fields a recorded turn carries. Never invent a field: where a needed field is not recorded, report `insufficient evidence` for that gate and say so in your final summary.

1. S6 is printed by `_request_lines` but ignored by the pass Boolean in `report()`. Make S6 a real gate with the same status vocabulary as the others (PASS, FAIL, insufficient evidence); the report line must begin `S6: PASS`, `S6: FAIL` or `S6: insufficient evidence`. The run passes only if it is complete and S1-S6 all PASS; missing budget evidence is insufficient evidence, never PASS. Keep REQUEST_BUDGET as is (never raise a budget to pass). If recorded turns also carry request counts for the shared recovery or item-facts calls, include them in the budget check; if the runner records none, do not invent them, and add a line `S6 note: item-facts and shared-recovery request counts are not recorded` so the gap is visible.

2. `_clues_recovered` treats a selected knowledge id as proof of recovery, and S3 counts a persistent `facts_after` fact on every later turn as a new assertion. Replace this with typed, committed evidence: S1 passes the recovery only when the find turn is committed AND the recovery fact `bench_clues_recovered` is present in that turn's recorded facts (use `_fact_after` over `facts_after`), plus the existing carried-by-Kristin world check; a selection of `k_sl_1b_d_r1` alone is no longer enough. S3 counts false-to-true transitions of the recovery fact: a turn is a new recovery assertion only when the fact is absent from the previous turn's facts (or there is no previous turn) and present in this turn's. S3 passes only when there is exactly one transition and it is at turn index 1, the fact never goes true to false to true, the recovery knowledge id is not selected again on any later turn (no repeated delivery), and custody is unchanged after the find. A digest change alone must never be used to say which fact changed.

3. S2 scans every serialized prompt and response, which can include the game's private selector or matcher traffic. If the recorded prompts or provider responses carry a field that distinguishes the narrator request and the complete player text from private selector traffic, make S2 judge only narrator requests and the complete player text, and report any private selector hits on a separate line that does not fail S2. If the rows carry no such distinction, keep the current scan scope unchanged, add the line `S2 note: private selector traffic is not separable in these rows`, and say so in your final summary. Do not add any reply parser; the human reads the prose.

4. TESTS: extend `tests/test_hidden_clues_smoke_report.py` with a clean three-replicate report that passes S1-S6, and single-fault fixtures (each failing exactly one gate): missing budget fields (S6 insufficient evidence), an over-budget turn (S6 FAIL), recovery selected but not committed or absent from facts (S1 FAIL), recovery fact persisting on later turns (S3 still PASS, not a second assertion), duplicate delivery on a later turn (S3 FAIL), and private versus public payload separation if you implemented it in item 3. Update existing fixtures that relied on selection alone as recovery evidence. Keep the existing tests for S4, S5, call-cap, drain exclusion and incomplete runs.

5. RUNBOOK: in `docs/testing-runbook.md` section 3, replace IN PLACE (do not append, do not add dates or a new entry, do not make the file longer than it is now) the sentence `For an authored-handoff turn it contains no candidate ID, candidate statement, `delivery_text`, `must_convey`, or grounding instruction.` with: `For an authored-handoff turn, private candidate metadata stays out of the narrator request. The selected delivery sentence may be shown as the text the game will append. Check the complete player text after runtime composition, including delivery and cues.` Keep the phrases `text the game will append` and `complete player text after runtime composition` each on a single line (the check greps for them line by line; rewrap the surrounding paragraph however you like).

HOW TO VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH: run `bash /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/check_t9h_stage2_smoke_report_repair.sh`. Do not edit the check. When done, print a short summary: what changed, and every place where a needed typed field was not recorded and the gate therefore reports insufficient evidence or keeps its old scope.
